questions.question: Which way of organizing AR software tools distinguishes desktop AR applications from mobile AR applications?
options: Marker-based application type
Developer skill
Tracking technology
Target application platform
questions.explanation: AR software tools can be categorized by target application platform, such as desktop AR applications or mobile AR applications.

questions.question: In the AR skill-based hierarchy ordered by decreasing programming skill, which category is placed last?
options: Plugins for existing developer tools
Low-level software libraries or frameworks
Standalone AR authoring tools
Rapid prototyping tools
questions.explanation: The skill-based hierarchy ends with standalone AR authoring tools, which assume no programming ability and can be used without any knowledge.

questions.question: Which AR software category requires strong programming or coding ability and understanding how to call library functions?
options: Standalone AR authoring tools
Low-level software libraries or frameworks
Rapid prototyping tools
Plugins for existing developer tools
questions.explanation: Low-level software libraries or frameworks require strong programming or coding ability and an understanding of how to call library functions.

questions.question: What skill is specifically required for plugin-based AR software tools?
options: Some programming ability and design prototyping skills
Skill with the original developer tool
No programming ability
Strong programming or coding ability
questions.explanation: Plugins require skill with the original developer tool with which the plugin is used.

questions.question: Why do low-level AR libraries or frameworks demand the most developer skill?
options: They expose plugin features that mainly require knowledge of an existing developer tool.
They expose core tracking and display functionality needed to build an AR application.
They expose authoring tools that assume no programming ability.
They expose only simple prototype visuals that can be shared with clients before coding.
questions.explanation: Low-level AR libraries and frameworks require the maximum skill because they provide access to the core tracking and display functionality used to build an AR application.

questions.question: What is ARToolKit mainly designed to provide?
options: Realistic scene rendering and interaction support for a complete AR application.
A standalone AR authoring tool that requires no programming.
Tracking support that lets a developer perform tracking and then carry out a related activity.
Mobile-only computer-vision tracking without any desktop support.
questions.explanation: ARToolKit is primarily a tracking-support library, and by itself it gives only primitive OpenGL rendering without built-in interaction or complex realistic graphics.

questions.question: What is the main benefit of combining ARToolKit with a scene-graph library?
options: ARToolKit handles tracking while the scene-graph library handles low-level object rendering, so the developer can focus on interaction.
The scene-graph library handles tracking while ARToolKit handles realistic rendering.
The combination provides only low-level OpenGL rendering and still requires writing interaction from scratch.
The combination removes the need for tracking because the scene graph can detect markers.
questions.explanation: When ARToolKit is combined with a scene-graph library, the scene graph takes care of low-level object rendering while ARToolKit remains responsible for tracking.

questions.question: What is a scene graph in computer graphics?
options: A GPS sensor stream used for outdoor tracking of a mobile AR device.
A node-based tree of nodes and links that represents a graphics scene and lets developers manipulate selected nodes.
A low-level OpenGL function that renders a 3D object directly to the screen.
A marker image used by ARToolKit to recognize the camera position.
questions.explanation: A scene graph is a node-based graph, essentially a tree of nodes and links, that represents a computer graphics scene and allows selective work with nodes to manipulate the scene.

questions.question: In the marker-cow AR example, what are the separate roles of ARToolKit and OSG?
options: ARToolKit tracks the marker, while OSG performs 3D registration and creates the rendered cow.
Both ARToolKit and OSG jointly track the marker and jointly render the cow.
OSG tracks the marker and performs 3D registration, while ARToolKit creates and renders the AR scene.
ARToolKit tracks the marker and performs 3D registration, while OSG creates and renders the AR scene with the cow.
questions.explanation: In the marker-cow example, ARToolKit handles tracking and 3D registration, while OSG handles creation of the AR scene with the rendered cow.

questions.question: Why are rapid prototyping and development tools used for an AR idea before major development?
options: To provide maximum development flexibility through low-level library access
To build a final high-performance AR application with realistic graphics
To replace a tracking library with a complete scene graph renderer
To visualize the idea with simple means and show it to end users or clients
questions.explanation: Rapid prototyping tools are used to visualize an AR idea simply and show it to users or clients before major development, so an unsuitable idea does not require further coding.

questions.question: What is FLAR Toolkit in relation to AR Toolkit?
options: A scene graph library used to manage rendering nodes
A 3D graphics library that can be paired with FLAR Tracker
A version of AR Toolkit ported to Adobe Flash
A non-Flash authoring tool for desktop and mobile AR
questions.explanation: FLAR Toolkit is described as a version of AR Toolkit ported to Adobe Flash, allowing an AR experience to run from within a web browser.

questions.question: What can a user accomplish in FLAR Toolkit with a few lines of code?
options: Activate a camera, track AR markers, and overlay virtual content onto the tracked image
Combine an AR tracking library with a 3D graphics library for full development
Generate markerless AR content using natural feature tracking
Write interaction from scratch for a complete realistic AR system
questions.explanation: FLAR Toolkit lets a user activate a camera, track AR markers, and load and overlay virtual content onto the tracked image for 3D registering with minimal effort.

questions.question: What is FLAR Manager primarily designed to do?
options: Provide low-level AR functionality with maximum development flexibility
Combine AR tracking libraries with 3D graphics libraries for prototyping
Supply markerless tracking and interaction support in a low-level library
Replace Adobe Flash with a non-Flash authoring tool for final production
questions.explanation: FLAR Manager is a framework that combines various AR tracking and graphics libraries, and such combinations are used primarily for prototyping rather than full-fledged development.

questions.question: Why might non-Flash-based AR authoring tools be less popular than Flash-based AR prototyping tools?
options: Flash-based tools have greater market penetration
Flash-based tools require more programming skill
Non-Flash tools cannot visualize an AR idea before major development
Non-Flash tools are limited to markerless augmented reality
questions.explanation: Non-Flash-based authoring tools for AR prototyping exist, but they may be less popular than Flash-based tools because Flash-based tools have greater market penetration.

questions.question: Why can a tracking-focused low-level AR library by itself produce only a rudimentary AR system, and what role can a scene graph library take in a combined AR framework?
questions.reference_answer: Low-level AR toolkits such as ARToolKit primarily provide tracking and only low-level primitive OpenGL rendering, with no built-in interaction or complex realistic graphics, so a complete realistic application requires writing interaction from scratch. A scene graph library can take care of low-level object rendering, allowing the developer to focus on interaction while ARToolKit remains responsible for tracking.

questions.question: How does the skill-based hierarchy of AR software tools order categories from the most to the least programming skill, and why can rapid prototyping tools be useful before major development?
questions.reference_answer: The hierarchy places low-level software libraries or frameworks first, then rapid prototyping tools, plugins for existing developer tools, and standalone AR authoring tools, according to decreasing programming skill. Low-level tools require strong programming or coding ability and understanding of library functions, while rapid prototyping tools need some programming or design prototyping skill, plugins require skill with the original developer tool, and standalone authoring tools assume no programming ability. Rapid prototyping tools are useful because they let an AR idea be visualized with simple means and shown to users or clients, so an unsuitable idea does not require further coding.

questions.question: How do tracking and three-dimensional registration work together in a marker-based AR example where a phone detects a marker and a 3D cow appears, and how can ARToolKit and Open Scene Graph be assigned to those tasks?
questions.reference_answer: In marker-based AR, a marker placed in the real environment triggers the augmented experience when a device detects it, so digital content appears at the marker's position. In the marker-cow example, tracking recognizes the marker and its position, while three-dimensional registration creates and renders the cow at that position. Combining ARToolKit with Open Scene Graph can assign tracking and three-dimensional registration to ARToolKit and the creation of the rendered AR scene with the cow to Open Scene Graph.

questions.question: How can AR software tools be categorized by platform and tracking technology, and what do DroidAR and Vuforia show about mobile AR tracking choices?
questions.reference_answer: AR software tools can be categorized by target application platform, such as desktop or mobile AR applications, or by tracking technology, such as computer-vision-based tracking or other sensors like GPS. Mobile-specific AR frameworks include ARToolKit for mobile, DroidAR, and Vuforia. DroidAR uses sensors for tracking support, while Vuforia uses computer vision for tracking support. ARToolKit for mobile is a mobile version of ARToolKit available for the iPhone operating system and Android and integrated with Open Scene Graph.
